output.decision: Do not launch a multivariate hero/offer/checkout test this month. With 3,000 monthly sessions and a 2% baseline conversion rate (about 60 purchases/month), splitting traffic across multiple combinations is unlikely to produce a decision-quality result. Run one prioritized, isolated A/B test instead after forming an evidence-backed hypothesis.
next_steps: Choose one high-impact area—preferably hero or offer—and define one primary metric: revenue per session, with conversion rate and average order value as guardrails.
Review qualitative and funnel evidence (session recordings, surveys, support tickets, analytics) to identify the largest customer objection or drop-off before selecting the change.
Write a hypothesis with the proposed change, expected outcome, rationale, audience, and stopping/sample-size rules.
QA tracking, checkout behavior, mobile rendering, offer logic, and experiment allocation before launch.
Run the single test across a representative period; defer multivariate testing until traffic and expected effect size support adequate sample sizes per variant.
missing_inputs: Minimum detectable revenue-per-session or conversion-rate lift and required confidence/power threshold.
Number and exact content of proposed hero, offer, and checkout variants.
Current funnel metrics by device and step, including checkout-start and purchase completion rates.
Research evidence supporting each proposed change, such as survey responses, recordings, and customer-service themes.

evidence_used.supports: The supplied source advises that multivariate testing is for high volume, emphasizes sufficient statistical power, recommends clear data-backed hypotheses, avoiding conflicting tests, QA, and prioritizing revenue per visitor/session over conversion rate.

assumptions: General quantitative basis: 3,000 monthly sessions at 2% conversion implies roughly 60 monthly purchases before any traffic split.
A multivariate test of hero, offer, and checkout would create multiple combinations and materially reduce observations per combination.
The source is unverified guidance; its stated 50,000–100,000-session range should not be treated as a universal requirement without a formal sample-size calculation.
